advisory.finding: The new pytest.skip in test_the_installed_pandoc_matches_the_legacy_fixture_provenance fails open. On any host whose platform key is not pinned, it skips the whole provenance check, including the platform-independent checks on the fixture's version and fingerprint map. Before this change, validate_pandoc_provenance raised 'unsupported Pandoc platform' there. If a gating platform drifts (for example a CI runner moves to linux-arm64, or darwin-x86_64), the test now reports a skip instead of a failure.
scenarios: A gating Linux job moves to an arm64 runner: the provenance test skips instead of failing with 'unsupported Pandoc platform'.
The fixture's pandoc version or fingerprint map drifts: on any unpinned host this is no longer detected, because the skip happens before those checks.
advisory.suggested_fix: Skip only on Windows, e.g. `if sys.platform == "win32": pytest.skip(...)`, or keep this one test in a Windows deselect argfile. Do not skip on every platform missing from ACCEPTED_PANDOC_BINARY_SHA256.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Keep the leading separator in the scratch-dir suffix assertion, e.g. `endswith(os.sep + os.path.join(".rebar", "scratch"))`, or compare Path parts.
evidence: Diff: `assert scratch.base_dir(repo_root=str(p)).endswith(os.path.join("", ".rebar", "scratch"))` replaces `.endswith("/.rebar/scratch")` (two places).
os.path.join("", ".rebar", "scratch") == ".rebar/scratch" on POSIX: an empty leading component adds no separator.
advisory.finding: The replacement assertion `.endswith(os.path.join("", ".rebar", "scratch"))` is weaker than the original `.endswith("/.rebar/scratch")`. os.path.join with an empty first component adds no leading separator: it gives '.rebar/scratch' (or '.rebar\scratch' on Windows). A base dir ending in, say, 'foo.rebar/scratch' would now pass.
scenarios: A regression that makes the scratch dir '<root>/x.rebar/scratch' or '<root>.rebar/scratch' still passes.
